Playing it

ControlWhat it does
6 top buttonschoose channel 1–6 (lit: chosen; glowing: sounding). On a channel's page, another channel shows same page; chosen channel again: its main view. From any other page, back to channel.
SELECT knobchosen channel's LEVEL: its fader. In most loops it is what makes them sing. 1 dB a detent up to −5 dB, then 0.1 dB a detent (−4.9, −4.8 …) up to +12 dB, where a loop's edge is. Below −60 dB: off.
ALGORITHM knobits PAN, 1 step a detent, L 50 … R 50. In a no-input mixer the pan shapes the sound, not only its place: in a loop through mix bus it is part of the loop.
KNOB 1–4on main view: GAIN, FREQ (middle filter's), LIMIT (loop's pitch), SEND 1; with SHIFT: NOISE, MID (middle filter's gain or width), PROTECT (overload protection), SEND 2. Dial covers screen while you turn. On a page: its 4 rows.
OCT− / OCT+channel's pages: MAIN, AMP, NOISE, EQ, SEND, FX (on SEQ's pages: through those). Their lights: a page that way.

SEQCOMPRESSOR, OUT, OUT EQ, OUT FX, then chosen channel's motion: LFO 1, LFO 2, MOD 1 TO 4, MOD 5 TO 8; then back to channel's page. On LFO and MOD pages a channel's button shows same page for that channel.

ARPOVERVIEW: 6 channels, their inputs and levels at once.
HOMEnew patch from any recipe (see New patches).
SHIFT + HOMEnew patch from recipe named in main view: the one playing, or the one PRESETS turned to.
HOME held 0.8 spatch nudged: every channel's tone moved a little, its connections and levels kept.

The main view

Chosen channel's number, very large, in its colour — in grey when the channel is not in the patch (muted, or nothing of it reaches anything: its LEVEL and SENDs off, with no RHYTHM); under it its input; under that patch's name (or a message, black on white; or MUTED, white on red); its meter, with a white bar where its fader is (red at left when fader is down); its pan along the bottom.

A channel

Left to right, as the app's block diagram:

input selector → + noise → GAIN → tube → FOLD → op-amp (and its overload protection) → HIGH, LOW → middle filter → brickwall limiter → mute → SEND 1, SEND 2 → LEVEL → insert effect → PAN → main mix

A page's rows show each parameter's name small, with a bar, and its value large under it. Hold SHIFT to see page's switches in place of its rows.

The input is what makes the loop:

InputLoopWhat makes it sing
PREchannel alone, from after its levelits LEVEL
POSTchannel and its insert effectits LEVEL; effect shapes the loop
MIX L / MIX Rside of mix bus: every channel feeding it, and returnsits LEVEL and PAN — and every other channel's
SEND 1 / SEND 2send bus: every channel feeding itits SEND
RET 1 / RET 2return bus: through rack's effects on sendsits SEND, through effects
NONEno loop: noise generator alone, through channel
CH 1 … CH 6another channel's output (after its insert): channels in a chain or ringeach channel's LEVEL round the ring

GAIN amplifies noise and loop. The tube shapes the sound as it rises (SATURATED drives it harder). The other 4 MODEs, the shapers, drive it as SATURATED does, into another curve: SPIRAL (after Airwindows' Spiral) rounds the peaks off, then folds them inward as it is driven harder, bright and buzzing; DENSITY (after Airwindows' Density) fattens; FUZZ has a sharp knee; HARD CLIP flattens peaks at full scale. None of them moves pitch. The op-amp amplifies it again and adds its own colour: 741 and OP07 are slow and dark, 4558 warm, CA3140 lopsided, TL072 and NE5532 clean. PROTECT sets threshold of overload protection: when op-amp's signal goes over it, the protection breaks the signal for a few milliseconds and the loop starts again from the noise, with the crackle no-input players know. Higher, it lets more through and the op-amp saturates more.

FOLD drives signal after tube into a wavefolder: past full scale it folds back instead of clipping, so the harder it is driven — by FOLD, by GAIN, by a loop growing — the more harmonics, never more level. It changes timbre only, never pitch.

LIMIT is brickwall limiter's speed. Its look-ahead is the delay that sets base pitch of a loop: fast (a fraction of a millisecond) gives high tones, slow (tens of milliseconds) low ones. The page shows it in milliseconds.

Filters set where a loop rings: a loop sings where its gain is highest, and a peak or band-pass is where you tune it. A loop can only ring at pitches its delay allows, so a narrow band-pass between them can keep a loop silent.

The rack

7 slots: slot 1–6 are channels', slot 7 output's (OUT FX). A slot's IN is OFF, INSERT (its channel's insert; slot 7: output's), SEND 1, SEND 2 or PREV (slot before it); its OUT is NONE, RET 1 or RET 2. An insert's output goes on through its channel, and to a return too if OUT says so.

DUCKDEPTHKEY: CH 1 … CH 6, MIX L, MIX R, SEND 1, SEND 2 — the louder it is, the quieter this
GATEDEPTHKEY: as DUCK's — the louder it is, the more this opens
CYCLESMODE: WAVELOSS (first n of every 8 cycles silent), SPUTTER (half-cycle now and then turned over or silent), WAVESET (each cycle repeated)AMOUNT
REEDNOTE, C2 … B5, a semitone a stepBREATH
OCTAVERMODE: ONE DOWN, TWO DOWN, BOTHTONE
DIFFUSERSIZE 1 … 8DENSITY
SAGTIME: window it averages over, 1.5 … 371 msDEPTH
CUTSUNIT, 10 … 46 msDENSITY
AUTO-LEVELLEVEL it holds, −30 … 0 dBSPEED
LP GATEDEPTHKEY: as DUCK's — opens it, closing slowly and darker
CROSSOVERMODE: DEAD ZONE, INSIDE OUTAMOUNT
FRICTIONSPRING: where it rings, 55 … 660 Hz, a stepFRICTION
GATELOPETHRESHOLD, −60 … −6 dBRELEASE
FREEZELENGTH, 50 … 371 ms (twice in LO-FI), a stepFADE: 0 frozen

RESONATOR is 6 tuned resonators on the root, in the chord's intervals, ringing about 1.2 s (after 4ms's SMR). In a loop it pulls feedback onto those notes and holds it there. Its ROOT and CHORD are steps and no LFO can move them: it steadies pitch, never glides it. XMOD (after Mutable Instruments' Warps) and DUCK / GATE (after its Streams) take a 2nd signal, so one loop can shape another: ring-modulate it, mangle its bits, duck it or open it in time with it.

Build 5's 6, all steady in pitch: CYCLES works on whole wave cycles between zero crossings — WAVELOSS drops some in a regular pattern (rhythmic holes a loop rebuilds itself through), SPUTTER turns half-cycles over or silences them at random (crackle), WAVESET repeats each cycle (time-stretched stutter that sinks into sub-drones). REED is a clarinet's bore and reed (after STK's Clarinet): signal is its breath, and it blows at its NOTE, which is a step and never moves. OCTAVER adds 1 or 2 octaves down, locked to signal by flip-flops on its zero crossings (after OWL's OctaveDown). DIFFUSER smears transients into a dense, metallic wash (Clouds' diffuser). SAG is a power supply starving (after Airwindows' PowerSag2): loud a while, gain sinks and comes back, so loops pulse and breathe; TIME is how long it remembers. CUTS cuts sound into phrases (3 3 2, 2 2 2 2 and the like); a cut plays on, or repeats what came just before it, whole or in halves or quarters — structured stutters after BBCut and Livecut. GLITCH is unchanged.

Build 20's 6, all steady in pitch too: AUTO-LEVEL follows a signal's loudness and turns it up or down to LEVEL, ±24 dB at most (after Befaco's Oneiroi): a loop held right at its edge without blowing up; SPEED is how quickly it follows. LP GATE is a low-pass gate (after Mutable Instruments' Streams): its KEY opens it, and it closes as a vactrol does, quickly at first, then slowly, darker as it closes, so loops decay like struck skins. CROSSOVER (after SuperCollider's): DEAD ZONE silences everything under AMOUNT, so loops burst and sputter out of silence; INSIDE OUT turns signal over, quiet loud and loud quiet. FRICTION is a mass on a spring, dragged by the signal (after SuperCollider's Friction): it sticks till the spring tears it off, then rings at SPRING's pitch until it catches again; low FRICTION rings, high drags, between them it creaks and rattles. GATELOPE (after Airwindows') is a gate that closes by sweeping its filters inward, treble down and bass up, till they meet: loops become decaying plucks. FREEZE loops its last LENGTH of sound: FADE 0 holds it frozen (nothing new comes in); above, new sound is laid over it and each pass fades a little.

PRESENCE is how much of the effect is heard; LO-FI halves its rate and its bits.

HOME's patches always feature the rack (build 22): 2 or 3 effects heard in every patch — inserts on heard channels at 55 … 100 % PRESENCE, often inside the channel's loop, or a loop through the rack — each a different effect, every effect a recipe has about as likely as the next. About half of patches also have an output insert (OUT FX, build 23), at 20 … 60 % PRESENCE, never a keyed effect (DUCK, GATE, LP GATE, XMOD) or REED.

The output

PageRowsWith SHIFT
COMPRESSOR (SEQ's first)AMOUNT (OFF .. 100 %), THRESH, RELEASE, SIDECHAIN (KICK or OFF)ATTACK, RATIO (2:1 .. 20:1, AMOUNT's share of it)
OUTLEVEL (main level), RET 1, RET 2, SPACE MIXKNOB 4: SPACE (ROOM, HALL, PLATE, CAVE, ABYSS, VOID)
OUT EQHIGH, LOW, GAIN, FREQKNOB 1: SHELF or CUT; KNOB 3: WIDE or NARROW

The COMPRESSOR works on the mixer's sound, before the drums join it, to hold its own against them. AMOUNT does it all at once: it compresses (that share of RATIO) and makes up the gain, so the mix comes forward, and with SIDECHAIN on KICK it ducks the mix under each kick (up to 18 dB) and lets it back over RELEASE: low AMOUNT, a little lift and a gentle pump; high, mix up front and a deep pump. Measured on host with a drawn patch: 35 % brings mix 5.6 dB forward and ducks it 4.7 dB under kick; 90 %, as far forward (output's headroom) and 12 dB under kick. OFF leaves mix untouched. A session keeps it; HOME does not touch it.

At top, SPACE MIX leaves reverb alone.

New patches

As on Tonitor: HOME draws a new patch from any recipe, so each press can be anything; SHIFT + HOME draws one from the recipe named in main view. That is the playing patch's recipe, or another: PRESETS turns through them from it, the name changing in place. Lilliput starts with a patch drawn from any recipe and a tempo drawn between 91 and 299 BPM, otherwise each time; a session loaded names its patch's recipe. A recipe is an archetype, not a preset: a kind of no-input sound, each with its own way of connecting channels, its own register, filters, tubes, op-amps, noises, effects and space — and its own motion, LFOs on parameters that make its character, drawn anew for each channel. Every draw comes out otherwise, in the recipe's direction:

Only what makes it sound is kept: 2 channels heard at least, faders past where loops singeach gesture to a destination drawn for each channel

HOME draws from any recipe; SHIFT + HOME from the one named. The patch's name, on main view, is its recipe's.

Faders are set a little past where each loop starts to sing, so a patch sounds at once and the faders are where the playing is. Some channels come with their fader down: brought up, they join in. For its first 2 seconds Lilliput plays into a new patch as a player would: a channel whose fader is up but which stays silent has its GAIN raised until it sings. Then it listens to output and sets main LEVEL so that every patch comes out about as loud, its peaks under −4 dB. After that a guard stays on: if the output holds at its ceiling, main LEVEL comes down a dB at a time. Faders are never touched.

HOME held 0.8 s moves every channel's GAIN, NOISE, filters, LIMIT and PROTECT a little, connections and levels kept: same patch, elsewhere.

Modulation

Each channel has 2 LFOs and 8 slots (Tonitor's modulation matrix, twice its slots). An LFO has SHAPE (SINE, TRI, SAW UP, SAW DN, SQUARE, STEPS — a new random value each cycle —, DRIFT — smooth random), RATE (0.01 … 20 Hz), MODE (FREE; ONSET: from start each time channel's loop bursts into sound; ONCE: 1 cycle from each onset) and FADE (in over up to 10 s from an onset). A slot takes a source — LFO 1, LFO 2, LEVEL (channel's own loudness: a loop that moves itself as it grows), OUTPUT (whole mix's), RANDOM (drawn at each onset) — to a destination — GAIN, NOISE, FREQ, MID, HIGH, LOW, LIMIT, PROTECT, LEVEL, PAN, SEND 1, SEND 2, channel's slot's 2 parameters and its mix, or either LFO's rate — by an amount, −100 … +100. The panel's values stay where you set them; the sound moves round them. Every new patch comes with its family's motion; SHIFT + SEQ throws chosen channel's modulation anew.

Rhythm

The RHYTHM turns the mixer into a rhythmic noise machine: it plays channels in time — gating them, choking them, striking them, pushing them — in structures drawn from a wide palette of styles.

Each channel gets a lane: its steps (up to 32), its step's length (1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 1/8 triplets, 1/16, 1/16 quintuplets, 1/16 triplets, 1/32), its hits and accents, how long a hit holds, how far the gate closes, each hit's chance, its chance of a roll (2 to 4 hits in a step) and its mutation (its steps flipping now and then, each round). Lanes of different lengths drift against each other (polymeter); lanes of different step lengths run in different time (polyrhythm). A lane plays its channel 1 of 4 ways:

  • CHOP — what you hear is gated: mutes and unmutes in time. The loop rings on behind the gate.
  • CHOKE — loop itself is gated: it dies between hits and grows back on each, a swell.
  • KICK — loop is choked, and struck at each hit by a burst of noise, pushed past its edge (+6 dB) while it is open: loop's own sound made a drum.

A channel in a ring (it takes another channel, or another takes it) is never choked: CHOKE and KICK gate what is heard instead, so the ring runs on behind the gate (choked, it died and never came back).

  • ACCENT — no gate: each hit pushes GAIN and FOLD up for a moment. A drone pulses in timbre, never in pitch.

SHIFT + the 2nd black key from the right draws a new rhythm for the patch as it is: the darkest loop gets the kick's part, the brightest the hats', those between the snare's and the percussion's; a channel with its fader down is left out, and now and then a drone is left free under it all. A loop slow to grow (slow limiter, narrow band-pass, loop through the sends) is chopped rather than choked. A sparse lane — open 1/5 of the time or less — is chopped too, over a bed 14 dB down, so its channel is never all but silent. Every recipe with every style sounds (host's test plays them all). Its key works as drums' key does: short, its pages (again: back); held 0.8 s, on or off; SHIFT + it, new rhythm.

TEMPO page (key, short): its title is the style playing (or RHYTHM OFF).

KNOB

MIX page (OCT+ from TEMPO, OCT− back): MIX sets how much of the gates is heard, against the loops as they run on: 100 % all gate (as before), 0 % loops alone, rhythm unheard. KICK's bursts and ACCENT's pushes follow it too.

A new patch keeps the rhythm playing (its lanes stay with channels); snapshots and sessions keep their own. The rhythm's changes — on, off, new one, tempo — are gestures like any other: the gesture loop records them.

Drums

Drum section beside the mixer, in the spirit of Bram Bos's Ruismaker Noir: synthesized, punchy and dirty, for rhythmic noise. 4 voices — KICK, SNARE, HATS, PERC (struck metal) — of a single engine, each with its own lane of steps, on RHYTHM's tempo and beat. Started, or given a new rhythm, they come in on the next beat; the RHYTHM's changes never disturb them, nor theirs the RHYTHM.

Black key 9 (3rd from right), short, opens their pages (again: back); held 0.8 s, they start or stop; SHIFT + it draws a new drum rhythm and plays it. On their pages:

  • white keys 1–4 choose KICK, SNARE, HATS, PERC (lit: the one chosen); SHIFT + one draws new sound for it, from its recipes; held 0.7 s, it is muted (its key blinks, dim; its page says MUTED), held again, back;
  • white key 16 (last, under SHIFT), held: BREAK, variation of rhythm playing, heard while held;
  • PRESETS goes through drum rhythms, a new one of each, playing;
  • OCT− / OCT+ through 3 pages.
PageRows (KNOB 1–4)With SHIFT
voice (its name and its sound's)TUNE (Hz), DECAY, DRIVE, LEVELSWEEP (how far above pitch it starts), ATTACK (HARD: sharpest transient; up to 100 ms: a soft one), NOISE (tone or noise), REVERB (its send into SPACE)
its 2nd pageBEND (how fast sweep falls), COLOR (noise filter), CLICK (burst on hit), PANMETAL (tone made metallic: off or 6 ratios), FILTER (low-, band- or high-pass)
drums' (their rhythm's name)SWING, VARIATION

A voice: tone, swept down in pitch, and noise through a filter, mixed by NOISE; envelope rising over ATTACK and falling over DECAY; CLICK on top; then DRIVE, a tanh up to 32 times over: every voice has its own. The dry drums go to the output after the reverb, so SPACE never washes them away; each voice's REVERB sends it into SPACE's reverb, heard even when mixer's SPACE MIX is down. Their level is their own: the trim that sets mixer's main level never moves it.

Sounds (SHIFT + a voice's white key draws one, its values anew each time): kicks DEEP, PUNCH, GABBER, SOFT (slow attack), TOM, SUB, CRUNCH; snares SNAP, NOISE, BODY, METAL, RIM, CRUSH, LONG; hats CLOSED, OPEN, METAL, SHAKER, TICK, CYMBAL, DIRT; percussion ANVIL, PIPE, SHEET, CLANK, CHAIN, SPRING, GRIND.

Rhythms (build 21: away from four on the floor). Each style is a way of building a rhythm, drawn afresh each time, so no 2 draws are alike. Lanes of different lengths drift against each other (polymeter); lanes of different step lengths run in different time (polyrhythm).

StyleHow it is built
AKSAKgroups of 2 and 3 added up to an odd meter, 5 … 13 (once, or twice with a changed 2nd half); kick and snare on group starts, perc limping on the 3s; now and then hats in 16 against it
PHASING1 cell on hats and on perc, perc's a step longer: they drift apart and meet again (after Reich)
EUCLID MESHeach voice a Euclidean rhythm of its own length (5 … 16), turned its own way
POLYRHYTHMeach voice its own subdivision: 8ths, triplets, quintuplets, 16ths at once
TIMELINEa bell's timeline (12/8 bell, clave, gahu, bossa, shiko, soukous; sometimes turned) against a pulse of the other kind
COLOTOMICcycles in cycles, after gamelan: a gong, ticks between, hats and snare interlocking
CASCADEa bouncing ball: hits ever closer; snare's ever farther
LIMPa long odd bar (18 … 28 16ths), the backbeat late, an 8th missing
DUSTa cloud: lanes of uneven lengths, every hit a chance
CANON1 figure, each voice entering it at another place
HOCKET1 dense line shared out, no 2 voices on a step
RITUALhalf time, slow: a kick, a snare far off, triplet hats
BROKENkicks off the beat, backbeat pushed or pulled, ghosts
TRIBALkick drawn Euclidean, dense, as toms are played; anvil 3 against 4
DIST BREAKa distorted break, straight
TEMPO CANON1 figure in several tempi at once: 8ths, triplets, 16ths, quintuplets, meeting now and then (after Nancarrow)

VARIATION (drums' page, KNOB 2) is how often a lane's round is played otherwise: a hit dropped, a pick-up before a hit, a hit pushed a step, an accent moved, a hit doubled, the lane turned, its 2nd half backwards, a round's rest (never the kick's). Each variant comes from the lane's own pattern, and the next round comes home, so the rhythm never wanders off. Each style draws its own amount, and each lane its own share of it (hats and perc more than kick). 0: every round as written; sessions from before build 21 load at 0.

A step can be more than a hit: accented, or ALT, its decay cut to 1/5 (closed hats among open ones, ghost snares). Nothing changes a voice's pitch: each voice keeps its TUNE on every step, in rhythms and in breaks, so the drums never turn into a melody (build 22; a session saved before with pitched steps loads with them level).

Break

On drums' pages, hold white key 16 (last, under SHIFT): drums play a variation of their own rhythm — fill, break, flams, beat repeat — for as long as it is held. Let go, rhythm carries on from where it would have been: nothing is written, each lane's steps run on underneath.

Each press draws one way, never the same as the one before, and keeps it while held; drum page's title names it. A break is quantized: it starts on the rhythm's next beat (next half bar for HALF TIME and MIRROR), playing as written until then, and fills are measured against the bar, so they land on its next downbeat however late they start. Every way is made from rhythm playing — its hits, accents and pitches — and from what each voice is:

WayWhat plays
STUTTERbar's busiest beat repeated: whole, then half, then a single step, ratcheting faster
AVALANCHEfill over the bar: snare from ghosts in 8ths to accented 16ths and doubles, kick on beats; lands on downbeat, all accented, and builds again
FLAMSrhythm as written, each kick, snare and perc hit flammed (soft grace note before it); accented snares dragged (2 graces)
DROPkick and snare out; hats and perc on, hats' gaps filled with ghosts
HALF TIMEkick, snare and perc at half speed; hats at full speed over them
CELL 3, 5, 6 or 7each lane loops a cell of that many of its own steps against the bar; kick keeps each downbeat
SWAPvoices trade lanes: kick plays snare's steps, snare kick's, hats perc's, perc hats'
MIRROReach half bar backwards; kick keeps its first step
TUMBLEperc on every step over 2 beats, from an accent down to ghosts, again and again; kick as written
INTERLOCKkick and snare keep 1st half of each beat, hats and perc the 2nd; after a bar they trade whole beats
SCATTERbar's 8 pairs of steps in another order, first in place
BUZZrhythm as written, hats in 3s then 4s, snare and perc doubled then tripled
GHOSTSevery gap filled with ghost notes, hats accented 3 3 2, kick pushing ahead of beat 4

The drums are not part of a patch: HOME, snapshots and gesture loops leave them alone. A session keeps them.

Gestures

Each channel has its own gesture loop. It records what your hands do to that channel — its knobs, its input key, its mute, its effect slot, channel thrown at random, a MIDI CC to it — and plays it back, round and round, while you go on playing over it. Loops are independent: each its own length, each started and stopped on its own. REC and PLAY act on chosen channel, and their lights show its loop.

  • REC arms channel's loop (screen says ARMED, REC blinks; its loop, if it plays, stops). Nothing is recorded until the channel changes: its first change starts recording (REC on screen, white on red, with seconds; REC lit). A loop it had is replaced: there are no overdubs, 1 loop a channel.
  • REC again ends it: loop is as long as from that first change to now, and plays at once (PLAY lit).
  • PLAY stops it, or plays it again from its start. Stopped, the channel stays where the loop left it.
  • REC held 1 s empties it.

Only 1 channel records at a time: REC on another channel ends recording (it plays) and arms that one. Each round begins from the channel as it was when its recording began — only what the loop touches — so it plays the same way every time; what you change that the loop does not touch stays yours. A new patch or a session stops the loops (PLAY plays each again, over new mixer). Up to 2048 changes among all loops, 10 minutes each. The output's, output slot's and RHYTHM's settings belong to no channel and are never recorded. The loops are kept with the session; a session saved before build 12, with 1 loop for all, loads as a loop for each channel it touched.

Snapshots

16 complete states of the mixer — every channel, every slot, output, modulation — kept with the session. SAVE (short) opens SNAPSHOTS page: the 16 as white keys lie, stored ones filled, last recalled framed.

  • white key let go soon: its snapshot recalled;
  • held 0.8 s: mixer stored in it;
  • SHIFT + it: emptied;
  • KNOB 1: MORPH time, off … 30 s. A recall then glides every value that can glide — levels, pans, gains, noise, filters, sends, limiters, protection, effects' parameters, returns, main level — from where it is to the snapshot's; the rest (inputs, types, routings, LFOs) changes at once.

SAVE again, or a channel's button, goes back.

Sessions

SAVE held saves the whole mixer as a session (64 of them); SHIFT + SAVE opens the sessions. A session keeps every parameter, channel chosen, patch's name and family, its 16 snapshots and its gesture loop.

Global setup and MIDI

SHIFT + SAVE held 0.8 s opens GLOBAL SETUP: MIDI (each channel's IN and OUT channel, AUTO for chosen channel, CC in and out on or off, USB and TRS ports), AUDIO (USB audio: STEREO, output, or CHANNELS, 6 channels each mono). A channel answers to and sends these CCs: 7 LEVEL, 10 PAN, 16 GAIN, 17 FREQ, 18 LIMIT, 19 SEND 1, 74 MID, 91 SEND 2, 92 NOISE.
